briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Weed Goes National While D.C. Stalls — Psilocybin Keeps Climbing
briefs.top: A Troy-built chain just became Arizona's biggest dispensary network, proof Michigan operators are punching above their weight even as the 24% wholesale tax squeezes margins at home — and a real repeal path is forming heading into November. Nationally, Compass Pathways edges closer to the first-ever FDA psilocybin approval and M&A dealmaking is heating up, even as a DEA judge hits pause on rescheduling yet again.

local.text: Michigan-born JARS becomes Arizona's biggest chain — JARS Cannabis, headquartered in Troy, signed a deal to acquire Sonoran Roots and its eight Ponderosa dispensaries, creating a 27-store network and the state's largest cannabis retailer.

Demand holds steady despite the new tax — Dispensary sales dipped only slightly in 2026, with the real driver being oversupply-driven price drops rather than the 24% wholesale tax, since operators are still sitting on roughly two years of flower inventory.

Operators get a real shot at tax relief — The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association endorsed GOP gubernatorial nominee John James after he pledged to repeal or sharply cut the 24% wholesale tax he says "drives up prices" and helps illegal operators.
Halloween season fuels fresh product drops — Michigan brands are rolling out seasonal SKUs like Armada Cannabis's 50 mg THC apple cider blends and live-rosin ciders to capture fall foot traffic.

Closures continue, but a workaround is emerging — Higher Love closed five of its nine U.P. dispensaries citing the wholesale tax, while fellow U.P. operator Rize kept growing by splitting the tax burden through negotiated supplier cost-sharing deals.

national.text: Compass Pathways inches toward a historic first — COMP360's Phase 3 COMP006 trial hit its primary endpoint with durable 26-week data, keeping the psilocybin drug on pace to potentially become the first FDA-approved classic psychedelic medicine as soon as late 2026.

DEA stalls again, but its own lawyers back Schedule III — A judge paused marijuana rescheduling hearings to weigh a new GAO report, with the government's response due Oct. 13, even as DEA's own filing continues urging the judge to "expeditiously recommend" moving cannabis to Schedule III.

Aggressive dealmaking is paying off for MSOs — Vireo Growth's buying spree, including its acquisition of Hawthorne Gardening from Scotts Miracle-Gro, helped drive revenue up more than 250% year-over-year.

Big MSOs push into Texas's growing medical market — Cresco Labs and Green Thumb Industries both entered Texas as its medical cannabis program expands, part of a broader buildout that's bringing the state to 15 vertically integrated operators.

Three psychedelic programs get an FDA fast lane — The FDA issued Commissioner's National Priority Vouchers to Compass Pathways' psilocybin program, Usona Institute's psilocybin program for depression, and Transcend Therapeutics' methylone for PTSD, compressing review timelines across the sector.
